corrections.what_happened: The run's manifest copied the value of the lane's API key, CLAUDE_API, because harness.provenance.settings_env took a secret only by the words in its name. The value is now "<set>", as the harness writes every secret.

rule.text:
1. A value is a credential when its name is CLAUDE_API (harness.chat._API_KEY), or holds
     PASSWORD, TOKEN, KEY or SECRET and does not end in _TOKENS (a limit counted in tokens), the
     names harness.provenance.settings_env names "<set>".
  2. Every such value in run_manifest.json and eval_manifest.json that is not "<set>" becomes
     "<set>", wherever in the file it stands; no other value changes.
  3. The value as recorded is kept nowhere, since it is a credential; each change names its place,
     and the sha256 of each file before and after are kept.
  4. After the change no file of the folder holds the value; otherwise nothing is written.

not_changed_and_worth_knowing: The value as recorded is kept in no file: it is a credential. The files' sha256 before the change are kept.
No other value of any file changes.

corrections.ordered_by: "resume and finish them, make sure they are all finished, correct, complete with all data, metadata and so on" (2026-10-26)
corrections.what_happened: 4 starts of the run answered questions and wrote no entry in legs: their processes were stopped, or their machine stopped, before they ended. Their rows carried the number of the next start that wrote an entry, so legs named fewer starts than wrote rows and gave those rows another start's settings.

rule.text:
1. A start is one log of starts.json: it began when its log was created and ended before the
     next start's log was created. A written entry belongs to the start whose span holds its
     started_at; each start holds at most one.
  2. A row belongs to the start whose span holds its timing.finished_at, a failure to the one whose
     span holds its failed_at, and must carry the number that start gave itself (rule above);
     otherwise nothing is written. The rows a start with an entry answered must be its n_answered.
  3. A start with no entry gets one: started_at the creation of its log, finished_at its last
     write, workers the number its log's first line names, n_answered its rows, aborted how its
     log ends (a process stopped from outside writes "exit -1" or no exit line), and from_its_log:
     the log, its embedder device and its last lines that name no question. Every other field of
     an entry is empty: not recorded.
  4. The entries are numbered again in the order of their starts; each row's and failure's leg is
     the new number of its start. No other value changes.

not_changed_and_worth_knowing: A rebuilt entry's started_at is when its command was launched (its log's creation), before the harness began; a written entry's started_at is when the harness began.
A rebuilt entry's code, flags, switches and settings are not recorded and stay empty; the rows' own call records hold the device each embedding ran on.
No answer, context, score, call record or time changes.

corrections.ordered_by: "resume and finish them, make sure they are all finished, correct, complete with all data, metadata and so on" (2026-10-26)
corrections.what_happened: The run's starts recorded no code version: git gave no answer in the shell they ran in on the desktop. The commit each one ran on is the one its clone's HEAD named when it began, by the clone's own reflog.

rule.text:
1. A start (an entry of legs) is corrected when its code_version.commit is empty.
  2. Its commit is the one the clone's HEAD moved to last before the start's started_at, by the
     reflog, and its branch the one the reflog's last checkout before then moved to. dirty and
     code_state stay empty: whether the working copy differed from the commit, and how, is not
     recorded.
  3. A start that recorded its commit must be the commit rule 2 gives for it; otherwise nothing is
     written.
  4. The run's top-level code_version is its last start's, as the harness writes it.

not_changed_and_worth_knowing: Whether a start's working copy differed from its commit, and how, is not recorded: dirty and code_state stay empty. A start whose git answered may show that it did.

checks.what: rule 3: each start that recorded its commit is the commit the reflog gives for it

evidence.what: the clone's reflog, written on the machine that ran the starts
